chapters.screenText: Run the supplied ISSM shelf and save its native results.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package.
chapters.expectedResult: Start with a connected cloud account, configured MATLAB license and required Connector.
chapters.title: Your goal: run the native ISSM example
instructions: Launch SquareIceShelf with its supplied inputs, inspect speed and save the results ZIP.
Start with an approved cloud account, configured MATLAB license and any required Connector.
chapters.note: Use the separate account and MATLAB guides if these prerequisites are not ready.
chapters.why: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package.

chapters.screenText: Start here in CryoLauncher. Choose Cloud for this tutorial.
chapters.screenWhy: Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.
chapters.expectedResult: Your workspace keeps scripts, datasets, run history and results together.
chapters.title: Start here
instructions: Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
chapters.note: Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.
chapters.why: Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.

chapters.screenWhy: Basic keeps the supplied scientific workflow and exposes its reviewed controls.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep runme.m as the Run target; no script upload is needed.
chapters.title: 1. Choose the Basic shelf case
instructions: Choose Cloud → Basic → ISSM → SquareIceShelf.
Basic uses the supplied example; no script upload or workspace clone is needed.
chapters.note: Keep the Run target as runme.m.
chapters.why: Basic keeps the supplied scientific workflow and exposes its reviewed controls.

chapters.screenText: Keep the supplied inputs and leave optional overrides disabled.
chapters.screenWhy: Basic retains the supplied example; optional edits change its scientific input definition.
chapters.expectedResult: The 1,000 km shelf tapers from 1,000 m to 300 m along y.
chapters.title: 2. Keep the supplied scientific inputs
instructions: Leave the optional Basic overrides disabled.
The 1,000 km square shelf tapers from 1,000 m to 300 m along y and solves a steady SSA stress-balance problem.
chapters.note: The four supplied files are runme.m, Square.par, DomainOutline.exp and Front.exp.
chapters.why: Basic retains the supplied example; optional edits change its scientific input definition.

chapters.screenText: Check Account connected and Storage, Containers and Compute Ready.
chapters.screenWhy: Storage, image, compute and MATLAB access must be ready before AWS can execute the model.
chapters.expectedResult: Use Prepare cloud first if the account resources are not ready.
chapters.title: 3. Confirm cloud readiness
instructions: Check Account connected and Storage, Containers and Compute Ready.
Use Prepare cloud if your account resources are not ready, then review again.
chapters.note: This run used 2 vCPU, 8 GiB and a 60-minute time limit.
chapters.why: Storage, image, compute and MATLAB access must be ready before AWS can execute the model.

chapters.screenWhy: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.
chapters.expectedResult: Reviewing shows the configuration before a paid run is submitted.
chapters.title: 4. Open the review
instructions: Choose Review & Launch.
chapters.note: Reviewing shows the configuration before a paid run is submitted.
chapters.why: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.

chapters.screenText: Confirm ISSM, SquareIceShelf and the tested image/digest.
chapters.screenWhy: The tested image and pinned digest identify the native software environment.
chapters.expectedResult: AWS charges the connected account; the displayed price is an estimate.
chapters.title: 4. Check the native case and image
instructions: Confirm ISSM and SquareIceShelf in the review.
Check the tested container image and pinned digest.
chapters.note: AWS charges the connected account; the displayed price is an estimate.
chapters.why: The tested image and pinned digest identify the native software environment.

chapters.screenText: When every readiness row is Ready, choose Launch cloud run.
chapters.screenWhy: This final confirmation submits a paid job to the connected AWS account.
chapters.title: 5. Submit the reviewed run
instructions: When all readiness rows are Ready, choose Launch cloud run.
chapters.note: Check the ISSM runtime row before confirming.
chapters.why: This final confirmation submits a paid job to the connected AWS account.

chapters.screenText: Wait for the submission and execution summary.
chapters.screenWhy: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.
chapters.title: 5. Wait for the submission confirmation
instructions: CryoLauncher stages the inputs and submits the native job.
The execution summary retains ISSM, SquareIceShelf and runme.m.
chapters.note: The script requests two MPI processes.
chapters.why: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.

chapters.screenText: Let the native job complete, then open its results.
chapters.screenWhy: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
chapters.expectedResult: Submission → start: 214.4 s; Batch task: 42.8 s.
chapters.title: 6. Let the native job finish
instructions: Allow the job to complete, then open its results.
Submission → container start: 214.4 s. Batch task: 42.8 s.
chapters.note: Long setup, queue and observation waits are shortened in this guide.
chapters.why: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.

chapters.screenWhy: A completed native job and its recorded provenance provide execution evidence.
chapters.expectedResult: MATLAB R2024b Update 7 · ISSM 2026.1 · exit code 0.
chapters.title: 6. Confirm native completion
instructions: The job succeeded with native exit code 0.
Runtime provenance records MATLAB R2024b Update 7 and ISSM 2026.1.
chapters.note: The configured license path supported native execution.
chapters.why: A completed native job and its recorded provenance provide execution evidence.

chapters.screenText: In Results select StressbalanceSolution → Vel; Render when needed.
chapters.screenWhy: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.
chapters.expectedResult: The first field may preview automatically.
chapters.title: 7. Render a speed field
instructions: Open Results, select StressbalanceSolution → Vel, then use Render when needed.
chapters.note: The first field may be previewed automatically.
chapters.why: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.

chapters.screenText: Read the field summary before interpreting the map.
chapters.screenWhy: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.
chapters.expectedResult: Four physical arrays, 91 mesh vertices and 148 triangles.
chapters.title: 7. Read the field summary
instructions: Vel contains 91 nodal speed values.
The native mesh has 91 vertices and 148 triangles.
chapters.note: The four physical arrays are Vx, Vy, Vel and Pressure.
chapters.why: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.

chapters.screenText: Open the full saved velocity PNG.
chapters.screenWhy: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
chapters.expectedResult: Speed: 0–9034.387288 m/year; x and y are metres.
chapters.title: 8. Inspect the full saved velocity map
instructions: Open the full saved Vel PNG.
Colour is speed in m/year; x and y are metres. Speed spans 0–9034.387288 m/year.
chapters.note: 10⁶ m equals 1,000 km. The saved PNG is unchanged.
chapters.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.

chapters.screenText: Read the convergence count as a diagnostic, rather than time.
chapters.screenWhy: A steady diagnostic convergence count is different from a transient time axis.
chapters.title: 9. Separate the diagnostic from time
instructions: The native convergence count is 23 steps.
It describes steady stress-balance convergence, not 23 transient timesteps.
chapters.note: Vel agrees with hypot(Vx, Vy); all four physical fields are finite.
chapters.why: A steady diagnostic convergence count is different from a transient time axis.

chapters.screenWhy: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
chapters.expectedResult: Wait for a fresh archive link for this run.
chapters.title: 10. Generate your result download
instructions: Choose Download results.
chapters.note: Wait for the fresh archive link for this run.
chapters.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.

chapters.screenText: Open the generated HTTPS link and save the ZIP.
chapters.screenWhy: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep its 11 members: fields, mesh, model, figure and provenance.
chapters.title: 10. Save the complete archive
instructions: Open the generated HTTPS link and save the ZIP.
The package includes native fields, mesh, final MATLAB model, figure and provenance.
chapters.note: This archive contains 11 members and passed its CRC check.
chapters.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.

chapters.screenText: Keep the four source files and results together.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep the source, versions, hashes and scientific qualifications with the result.
chapters.expectedResult: All four physical fields and the mesh match the declared reference exactly.
chapters.title: Keep the inputs and results together
instructions: Retain the four source files, result ZIP, versions, hashes and saved MATLAB RNG state.
All four physical fields and the mesh match the declared reference exactly.
chapters.note: This is the supplied synthetic diagnostic case; it is not a field-data forecast.
chapters.why: Keep the source, versions, hashes and scientific qualifications with the result.
